name: Sylvan Learning
benefit: Daily practice, not by the hour
line: Sylvan tutors in booked sessions, priced by the hour. AMP gives daily practice at home for $59 a month.
description: AMP vs Sylvan Learning: a live tutor at about $50 an hour, or adaptive math practice at home every day for $59 a month. What each offers and has shown.
verdict: Sylvan Learning puts a live, Sylvan-certified teacher with a child, at a local center or online [1], and we think a good tutor is hard to beat. Its sessions typically average $50 to $55 an hour [3]. For $59 a month, AMP finds the level in each strand of math, explains every answer and brings old skills back on a schedule, any day, at home.

reasons.title: A month of AMP costs about one Sylvan hour
reasons.body: Sylvan's sessions, online or in person, typically average $50 to $55 an hour [3]. At its centers, each independently owned location sets the price, and a typical start is $50 or more per session [2]. AMP is $59 a month or $599 a year for unlimited practice, and the first 100 answers are free. By our arithmetic, four one-hour sessions a month at those rates come to $200 or more.

reasons.title: Practice any day, with no appointment
reasons.body: Sylvan teaches in scheduled sessions, in person at a center or live online [1]. To begin, a parent requests the free assessment, and the center makes contact within one business day [1]. AMP starts the same day without a card, at home, in any current browser. Practice can happen any day the learner is ready.

reasons.title: Placement happens inside practice, in 14 strands
reasons.body: Sylvan places a child with a free Insight Assessment that covers a single subject, and builds a personal plan from it [1]. AMP has no separate test. It finds the level in each of 14 strands of math within the first 24 problems, then updates the estimate with every answer. A learner can be strong in geometry and still get practice aimed at fractions.

reasons.title: Old skills come back on a schedule
reasons.body: AMP brings each learned skill back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics, and a miss resets the schedule. We found no review schedule on Sylvan's math tutoring pages [1]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed, spaced practice scored 62% on a surprise test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [8]. The researchers wrote the test, and the mixed practice was also spaced.

reasons.title: The rules are public, and help never counts
reasons.body: Sylvan says its program adapts to a child's skill level and pace [1], but we found no mastery rule on its pages. AMP's rule is written down and in public code: four of the last five answers right without help. An answer given after a hint or the lesson does not count, and two misses in a row send practice back to what the skill builds on.

rows.price: Set by each center: a typical start of $50 or more per session [2]. Sessions typically average $50 to $55 an hour [3]. Most families choose monthly memberships [1].
rows.buyers: Families, through a local center. Each location is independently owned and operated and sets its own price [2].
rows.range: Kindergarten through grade 12, from homework help to pre-calculus [1].
rows.start: A free Insight Assessment, one subject per assessment, that leads to a personal plan [1].
rows.teaching: A live Sylvan-certified teacher, in person at a center or, at many centers, online, following the child's personal plan [1].
rows.next: The personal plan from the assessment, which Sylvan says adapts to a child's skill level and pace [1].
rows.mastery: No mastery rule found on its math tutoring pages [1].
rows.review: No review schedule found on its math tutoring pages [1].
rows.adult: Requests the free assessment, picks a membership with the local center, and schedules sessions [1].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site. Evidence for ESSA has an entry named SylvanSync Mathematics, without a rating [6]. Its growth claim names no study [4].

theirs: Sylvan Learning is a tutoring brand with local centers and live online sessions [1]. Its site describes its centers as locally owned [5], and says Sylvan has helped students and families for over 40 years [4]. This page is about its math tutoring.

Math tutoring runs from kindergarten through grade 12, from homework help to pre-calculus, including algebra, fractions, geometry, trigonometry, and probability and statistics [1]. A child works with a Sylvan-certified teacher, in person at a center or, at many centers, live online, with the same personalized plan [1]. Sylvan presents it as support alongside school that follows school standards [1].
It starts with a free Insight Assessment in one subject. The local center then explains the plan and the options, and most families choose a monthly membership with no long-term contract [1].
credit: A live, Sylvan-certified teacher, in person or online [1]. A live teacher can listen, ask a question back and change course in the middle of a problem. AMP has no live teacher and no chat tutor.
A center to go to [1]. The work happens away from home, with an adult who is not the parent.
A free assessment to start, and a monthly membership with no long-term contract [1].
Homework help alongside school, from kindergarten through pre-calculus [1]. AMP follows its own sequence, not this week's school assignments.

theirs: Sylvan's about page says that, based on independent research, its students see "up to two to three times more academic growth" than other students [4]. The page names no study, sample or design, and the page links to no research. In our reading, an "up to" figure describes a best case, not a typical result.

As of November 2026, we found no outcome study of Sylvan's math tutoring on its site. Evidence for ESSA has an entry named SylvanSync Mathematics, which we take to be Sylvan's, with no rating and the note "No studies met inclusion requirements" [6]. We found no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report for it.

Tutoring as a method has strong evidence. A 2026 meta-analysis of 263 randomized trials found a pooled effect of 0.40 standard deviations, falling to 0.16 to 0.22 for large U.S. programs measured on standardized tests [7]. Those trials studied tutoring programs in general, not Sylvan.
ours: AMP is built on methods with strong evidence in math, applied at every problem. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged 0.49, against 0.05 for marking right or wrong only [9]. These are averages by feedback type across ages and subjects, not a head-to-head trial. Mixed, spaced practice scored 62% against 38% a month later, in a randomized trial of 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, on a test the researchers wrote [8]. AMP explains every answer and schedules every review, every day the learner practices. We expect that to show in outcomes, and we have committed to measuring it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each is registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your child works best with a person beside them, in a room or on camera.
You want an adult outside the family to plan the work and keep the schedule.
You want help with this week's school homework.
You want a local center and in-person sessions, and the hourly price fits your budget.
amp: You want practice at your child's level every day for about the price of one tutoring hour a month.
Your week has no room for drives or booked sessions.
You want every answer checked and explained, and old skills brought back on a schedule.
You want to read the exact rules the program follows.
Your child already has a tutor and needs practice between sessions.

questions.question: How much does Sylvan Learning cost for math?
questions.answer: Each center sets its own price. Sylvan's pricing page gives a typical start of $50 or more per session [2], and its online tutoring page says sessions average $50 to $55 an hour [3]. AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child.

questions.question: Has Sylvan shown that its tutoring works?
questions.answer: Sylvan's site says its students see up to two to three times more growth, citing independent research, but names no study [4]. We found no outcome study on its site, and the Evidence for ESSA entry named SylvanSync Mathematics has no rating [6].

questions.question: Can we use AMP and Sylvan together?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP is a separate program a family runs at home, with a hint, a lesson and worked steps for every problem. It has no live teacher, so it adds daily practice between sessions rather than replacing a tutor.
